summary: Interferon alfa-2b (Intron A) is a recombinant type I interferon used as an antiviral and antineoplastic immunomodulator for hairy cell leukemia, malignant melanoma (adjuvant), follicular lymphoma, AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma, condylomata acuminata, chronic hepatitis B and C. It carries a BOXED WARNING for severe or fatal neuropsychiatric, autoimmune, ischemic, and infectious disorders. Dosing and route (SC, IM, IV, intralesional) are highly indication-specific, and treatment requires close clinical and laboratory monitoring.
indications: Malignant melanoma - adjuvant therapy after surgery in patients at high risk of recurrence
Chronic hepatitis C (alone or with ribavirin)

dosage.d: 2 million IU/m2 SC or IM three times weekly
dosage.n: Up to 6 months; continue if responding

dosage.d: Induction 20 million IU/m2 IV on 5 consecutive days/week x4 weeks; maintenance 10 million IU/m2 SC three times weekly x48 weeks
5 million IU SC three times weekly for up to 18 months
30 million IU/m2 SC or IM three times weekly
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or maximal response

dosage.d: 1 million IU per lesion (up to 5 lesions per session)
dosage.t: Three times weekly on alternate days for 3 weeks

dosage.d: 3 million IU SC or IM three times weekly (often with ribavirin)
30-35 million IU/week SC/IM (5 million IU daily or 10 million IU 3x/week)

admin: Reconstitute powder per labeling; check appropriate vial strength and route for the specific indication
Routes vary by indication: subcutaneous, intramuscular, intravenous infusion, or intralesional
Administer at bedtime and premedicate with acetaminophen to reduce flu-like symptoms
Ensure adequate hydration, especially during high-dose IV induction
Withhold/reduce dose or discontinue for severe neuropsychiatric, hematologic, hepatic or autoimmune toxicity per label
Use with caution; rotate SC injection sites
moa: Interferon alfa-2b binds type I interferon (IFNAR) receptors, activating the JAK-STAT pathway and inducing transcription of interferon-stimulated genes. This produces antiviral effects (inhibition of viral replication via enzymes such as 2'-5' oligoadenylate synthetase and protein kinase R), antiproliferative effects on tumor cells, and immunomodulation including enhanced macrophage phagocytosis, augmented NK-cell and T-cell cytotoxicity, and upregulation of MHC class I expression.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to interferon alfa-2b or any component
History of severe psychiatric disorder when used with ribavirin (per combination labeling)
relative: Pregnancy and partners of pregnant women (with ribavirin)

preg: Avoid in pregnancy. Interferon alfa-2b has abortifacient (dose-related abortion) effects in pregnant rhesus monkeys. Use effective contraception. When combined with ribavirin, treatment is contraindicated in pregnancy and in male partners of pregnant women due to ribavirin's teratogenic/embryocidal risk.
lact: It is not known whether interferon alfa-2b is excreted in human milk in clinically meaningful amounts. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, decide whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, considering importance to the mother.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment (CrCl <50 mL/min); reduced clearance can increase toxicity. Monitor closely and reduce dose or discontinue if severe adverse reactions occur. Interferon plus ribavirin requires special caution due to ribavirin accumulation.
hepatic: Contraindicated in decompensated hepatic disease and autoimmune hepatitis. May cause hepatotoxicity and worsening of liver function; discontinue promptly if signs of hepatic decompensation (rising bilirubin, coagulopathy, encephalopathy) develop.

major: Telbivudine - increased risk of peripheral neuropathy; avoid combination
Ribavirin - hemolytic anemia and teratogenicity (combination-specific risks)
moderate: Theophylline - interferon inhibits CYP1A2, raising theophylline levels
CNS depressants and narcotics - additive neuropsychiatric effects
Live vaccines - reduced response / immunomodulation concern
minor: May affect CYP-metabolized drugs by reducing hepatic CYP enzyme activity
interactions.food: No specific food interaction; maintain good hydration.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - worsens hepatotoxicity and depressive/neuropsychiatric symptoms.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, elevated transaminases/bilirubin, hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism (abnormal TSH), and hypertriglyceridemia.

common: Flu-like syndrome (fever, chills, myalgia, fatigue, headache)

monitoring: CBC with differential and platelets at baseline and periodically (weekly during high-dose induction)
Thyroid function (TSH) at baseline and periodically
Neuropsychiatric status - screen for depression and suicidal ideation throughout therapy
Baseline and periodic ophthalmologic exam (especially with pre-existing eye disease)
ECG/cardiac assessment in patients with cardiac disease
counsel: Expect flu-like symptoms early on - take acetaminophen, dose at bedtime, and stay well hydrated
Report depressed mood, hopelessness or thoughts of self-harm immediately - this is a serious warning effect
Report shortness of breath, chest pain, vision changes, severe abdominal pain or signs of infection (fever, sore throat)
Use reliable contraception; avoid pregnancy during and after treatment (especially if combined with ribavirin)
Avoid alcohol; attend all blood test and follow-up appointments
Learn correct subcutaneous injection technique and rotate sites if self-administering
pk: Antiviral activity persists ~1-2 days; supports 3x/week dosing
Refrigerate 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze; protect from light
pearls: BOXED WARNING: may cause or aggravate fatal or life-threatening neuropsychiatric, autoimmune, ischemic, and infectious disorders - monitor closely and discontinue for persistently severe signs/symptoms
Screen for and monitor depression/suicidality throughout therapy
Dosing, route and units (million IU) are strictly indication-specific - always verify the regimen
Premedicate with acetaminophen and dose at bedtime to blunt flu-like syndrome
Largely replaced by direct-acting antivirals for chronic hepatitis C and by pegylated interferons for many indications
Reversible thyroid dysfunction is common - check TSH at baseline and during therapy
missed: If a dose is missed, administer it as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next scheduled dose; do not double the dose. For complex oncology regimens, contact the prescriber for guidance on rescheduling.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose may intensify dose-related toxicities (severe flu-like symptoms, profound myelosuppression, hepatic and neuropsychiatric effects). Discontinue the drug and provide intensive supportive care with monitoring of blood counts, liver function and organ systems until recovery.
